h.select_rule: Discard any hypothesis whose condition is the edited field's own current value, or whose condition merely disables or disconnects the edited component. From the rest, keep 10 with distinct mechanisms and field pairs, favouring those where an informed expert could plausibly bet on either direction.
h.strategy: Two patterns are banned because experts find them obvious: (1) conditioning on the current value of the same field being edited, which just restates that upgrading a weak setting helps more than upgrading a strong one; (2) conditions that make the edited component unused, unreachable or inert. Instead, each hypothesis must link two DIFFERENT fields that interact through a non-trivial mechanism, such as substitution between parallel routes, a capacity already supplied elsewhere, one part acting as a bottleneck for another, or interference that turns a usually helpful edit harmful. No condition setting may appear in more than two hypotheses. Use the gaps and negated assumptions as the source of each idea. In each 'why', name the mechanism and explain why the opposite direction is also a priori plausible.

hyps.why: When edge 4 already feeds a conv-processed signal into node 3, a second parallel conv on edge 5 adds diminishing marginal capacity at the output sum.
If the edge-5 input to node 3 is only a parameter-free pooled signal, edge 4 becomes the main learnable route to the output, so making it a conv matters more.
A deep node0->1->2->3 conv chain benefits more from a direct identity shortcut that preserves raw input and eases optimisation than a shallow cell does.
When edge 4 already supplies an identity-like route into node 3, converting edge 3 to a conv sacrifices less shortcut benefit while adding capacity.
Pooling node 1 features that were already pooled from the input compounds parameter-free smoothing along node0->1->2, especially harmful at 16x16 resolution.
With raw-input flow already guaranteed by the edge-3 residual, edge 0 can become a pure conv without losing the identity path, so its gain is larger.
Without the direct input-to-output edge, node 3 depends entirely on edges 4 and 5, so a conv on edge 5 carries more of the representational load.
Conv-processed node 1 features are worth refining further, and edge 4 then forms a genuine two-conv path to the output rather than a single conv on raw input.
When node 1 is only a pooled copy of the input, edge 1 provides node 2's main learnable transform, so making it a conv substitutes for missing capacity.
If edge 3 is a conv, node 3 has no near-identity input, so a skip on edge 4 supplies a short bypass that eases optimisation more than in cells that already have one.
